_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
EVERY FIELD HAS A WORD CAP, and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build past it:
name 16, why 40, risk 80, touches 80, note 120, comment 120, askedBy.detail 80. A
session with more to say than that puts it in the feature's Brief or history file
and links it. ONE FACT, ONE HOME: replace a sentence that is out of date; never append
an UPDATED paragraph beneath it. On 2026-09-03 one item's comment had grown to 1,388
words across seven sessions that way, and Mike could not read his own list.
activeOn: { machine, since } says which computer is working an item right now —
'laptop' or 'desktop', from the date given. Mike's instruction, 2026-09-03, after item
4.54 was built on both machines in the same week. Absent means nobody is on it. The
page shows it as a column, the control shows it on the row, and the control's save
carries it through. Shutdown clears or keeps it; startup reports the other machine's.
rankedByMike: false marks an item filed after orderedByMikeOn that Mike has not yet
placed. The page and the Handbook control show it. It clears itself: the control's
export does not carry the field, so his next saved list drops it.
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.

items.why: A firm manager who has customised nothing sees "Added here" against every observation point the mentor wrote, because the resolver returns the layer above untouched.

A firm manager is told they added a point they cannot edit and did not write, which is the opposite of what the badge exists to say — and the badge is what tells them whether a correction of theirs is safe from the mentor's later changes. It looks completely normal on screen, which is why nobody has reported it.

items.name: Economic analysis — the forecast asks the AI for market research
items.why: Mike's request, 2026-09-03: a tick reading "economic analysis" charging the AI to research global and local markets, because most three-way forecasts support funding requests. It would be the FIRST report model here to call the AI. Detail in report-models.md.
items.risk: AI text going into a document a bank reads. The standards require `isApproved: true` before AI output is committed for financial work, and a confident wrong claim about a market looks exactly like research. 🔴 PRIVACY NEEDS A FRESH RULING: useful research needs the client's industry and location, and "specialist importer in Nelson" identifies a business as surely as a name. The one PII exception granted (Meeting Review) says in terms it is no precedent.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-03 — "i want to include an option to tick 'economic analysis' which then charges AI to conduct global and local market research (i will give detailed instructions and prompt in future) such that they can be included in an overall report - since the majority of 3 way forecasts are used to support funding requests". items.name: International versus local — the forecast treats every sale and purchase as domestic
items.why: Mike's request, 2026-09-03: an international-versus-local split for purchases and sales on step 3, allowing for shipping and FX. Drawn 2026-09-04 and awaiting his approval; the drawing and its six rulings are recorded in ARTEFACTS.md.
items.risk: 🔴 THE GUARD THIS MUST NOT BE BUILT WITHOUT: with the tick off and both overseas series empty, the 10,155-cell golden test must produce byte-identical output, and it is written first — this change reaches into the GST computation, which the golden set covers cell by cell. GST is wrong in both directions today: every sale is charged, and every purchase credited when the supplier is paid, where exports are zero-rated and imports pay at the border.

items.note: Five sheets, read end to end: two supplier input sheets, an Index Tables lookup and Financial Projections. A supplier sheet turns a short input set into a payment schedule — 4,469 units, 693,271 of unit cost, a 415,963 deposit and 255,650 balance due across twelve 30-day bands, with balance interest and FX loss computed separately. ⚠ A CORRECTION MADE BY READING THE SHEET: the curves the supplier sheets actually consume are the FOUR-band table, each pattern totalling 100%; the seven-band area on Index Tables does not. Detail in the commit message of 8b550fe.

Do not start the build to see how it goes: the calendar conversion decides which month a payment lands in.

items.name: The book value of one asset is typed, because no screen asks for the asset schedule
items.why: Selling an asset needs its price and its book value; the gain between them is profit that month. The app holds six category totals, never individual assets. The figure lives on the Fixed Asset Schedule, which step 1 never requests.
items.risk: Nothing is broken while it is undone: the advisor reads the number off the same schedule the app would parse. The risk is in the doing, and it is 4.60's — a Fixed Asset Schedule varies far more between packages than a Balance Sheet, and only Xero has ever had a real export put through it. A schedule read wrongly gives a plausible book value, and that moves the gain, the tax and retained earnings together.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-03 — he challenged the typed field directly ("if i have a vehicle it must be listed in the asset schedule and balance sheet - which is paired to the depreciation rates - cant see why you cant pull the book value from that?"), was shown that the figure lives on a report the app never asks for, and chose: "typing it for now".

items.note: ⚠ COUPLED TO 4.60 AND SHOULD FOLLOW IT. 4.60 waits on four real exports from QuickBooks Online and MYOB to move those two packages from `expected` to `verified`, and whoever collects them should be asked for the Fixed Asset Schedule at the same time. It is the same request to the same person, and doing it separately means asking twice.
